Subject: Renewal uplift and mid-year capacity — options

Hi David,

We're working through our forecast and expect a mid-year usage jump. Before the renewal next April, procurement asked whether we can:

- do a temporary top-up now and annualize to the renewal period, or
- co-term new capacity to Jan 1 to align with our budget year.

Can you send a short options matrix (pricing per token / unit at current usage, top-up tranche prices, and a pro-rata invoice schedule)? Also need to understand any discount tiers you can apply for an uplift that gets us to ~1.6x our committed units.

Cc'ing procurement for visibility. Legal would likely want a short change-of-scope SOW if we move forward — happy to share comments.

Thanks,
Sylvia Park
Head of Platform
Brightwell AI

Hi Sylvia — thanks for the context. I put together three pragmatic paths (summary below) and attached a spreadsheet with line-item math.

Attachments:
- BW_pricing_v1.xlsx (XLSX) — line-item unit economics and invoice schedules
- Brightwell_SOW_v1.pdf (PDF) — short SOW template for a tranche top-up

Options (high level):
1) Temporary tranche top-up (fastest)
   - One-off top-up for the remainder of the quarter, invoiced immediately, priced at committed-rate + 8% uplift.
   - Can be smoothed as a voucher for future months if you prefer credits.
2) Annualize early (co-term to Jan 1)
   - Move the uplift onto the next annual contract and apply a 7% blended discount for committing to the full year early.
   - Pro-rata invoice for months remaining until co-term date.
3) Staged commitment (stepwise)
   - 60% of forecast uplift now at committed rate, remaining 40% as an optional top-up in Q1 with pre-negotiated discount bands.

Notes / asks:
- If procurement prefers annual invoicing, we can shift to an annual billing schedule but will need legal to sign the SOW variant.
- If you want a smaller short-term credit versus cash invoice, we can issue a voucher and reflect it on your next invoice.

Can we do a quick 30-min call tomorrow to walk through the numbers? If you prefer, I can loop in Sales Ops and Legal to firm up the invoice language.

Best,
David Kim

- Invoice cadence: procurement prefers 1x annual invoice aligned to Jan 1, but we need a pro-rata invoice for any consumption between now and the co-term date (ideally invoiced on your end but appearing as a single consolidated charge on our PO).
- Discount ask: given the growth visibility, can you do a 12% blended discount if we commit to convert the uplift to an annual add-on now? If not, what gate would get us to 12%?

Legal note: attached SOW_comments.docx with bullet edits — primarily around billing language and audit logs retention.

If you can send a short redline to the SOW and a single summary sheet that shows current committed, proposed uplift, blended annual rate, and resulting monthly invoice, we can move to internal approval next week.
